what: The rename collapsed two distinct behavior names in the node README into a one-preposition difference (connect BY invocation vs connect ON invocation). The CR's own oracle is one unambiguous name per concept, so the rename manufactured the ambiguity it exists to remove. Second behavior renamed to name what it does: register and take the claim on connecting.

A Given asserted the postcondition its own When establishes, leaving the scenario no observable transition. Pre-existing in form, made legible by the rename, and on a line this CR had already opened. Given reduced to the session-state precondition only; test vector unchanged, not a widening.

The new anti-role-play voice clause banned 'standing by', which is a terse status acknowledgment rather than simulated physicality — it is what the scenario's first clause actively rewards, so the tightening failed a conforming run and put two clauses of one boolean in tension. Phrase removed. Conductor sweep found the identical parenthetical in the node README, which the judge had not named; both sites fixed.

The conductor's automated rewrap demoted a peer Subject bullet to a nested sub-item, so the node README presented two behaviors as one-inside-the-other while its behavior table listed them as peer rows — the README contradicting itself one level below where round 1 found the same defect class. Introduced by the round-1 finding-A fix, not by the producer. Bullet dedented to column 0; all 12 Subject bullets verified at column 0 and no nested bold bullets remain in any touched file. Root cause: a scripted rewrap over a markdown list, which cannot see list semantics — hand-verify structure after any automated reflow.

Judge pre-flight noted sdd:builder-spec-governance absent from the producer's declared set; aced:aced-builder-spec unions onto the generic bar rather than replacing it, so both resolve as builder-spec candidates. Judge graded against the union and attributed no defect to the gap — a declaration gap, not a substantive one. Recorded rather than re-run.
